fyNote: Financial year ends 31 December. 1H = January to June 2026 (unaudited, from MISC's results release). Return on equity uses equity at December 2025. Next results: Q3 2026, due late November 2026.

sources.title: MISC results release, half-year to 30 June 2026

segmentNote: Four businesses; tankers (Petroleum & Products) earn the most revenue and profit (AR p.54; PR).

how.title: How MISC makes money
how.text: Revenue = long-term charter fees for ships and floating production units + freight from shorter voyages + shipyard project work

story.scale_label: ships, gas carriers, offshore units and a shipyard
story.debt_label: net debt at Dec 2025 (borrowings minus cash)

debt.label: net debt at Dec 2025 (borrowings minus cash)

items.label: Goods and services bought
items.tip: Fuel, port charges, crew services, ship repairs and shipyard materials.

items.label: Depreciation and impairment
items.tip: Wear and tear on ships and offshore units, plus write-downs of older vessels.

items.label: Employment costs
items.tip: Salaries for seafarers, yard workers and office staff.

items.label: Other items
items.tip: Items not split out in the value-added statement (balancing figure).

items.label: Tax
items.tip: Low, because shipping income is largely tax-exempt in Malaysia.

items.label: Profit to shareholders
items.tip: What is left for shareholders: paid as dividends or kept to grow the business.

pnl.incomeNote: FY2025 breakdown (AR p.76); the 2026 results release does not split costs. Plus about RM12.36 per RM100 of revenue from other income, interest, ship sales and other gains.

lines.label: Net finance costs, ship sales and other

fiveYear.note: Full years. First half 2026: revenue RM7.68bn (+38.8%) and profit RM1,896m (+62.0%), helped by very high crude tanker rates and gains on ship sales (PR).

rows.name: Petroleum & Products (AET tankers)
rows.tip: Oil and product tankers; the main driver of the jump in 1H2026 profit on high crude tanker rates (PR).

rows.name: Gas Assets & Solutions
rows.tip: LNG carriers on long charters; lower in 1H2026 after vessel disposals, lay-ups and lower rates (PR).

rows.name: Offshore
rows.tip: Floating production units leased to oil companies; higher construction revenue in 1H2026 (PR).

rows.name: Marine & Heavy Engineering
rows.tip: Shipyard building offshore structures and repairing ships in Johor; projects in higher construction phases (PR).

segments.note: Full-year 2025 split; the results release describes segment trends for 1H2026 but gives no segment figures.

assets.label: Ships, FPSOs, receivables and other assets

balance.note: Balance sheet at 31 December 2025 (the results release gives only net assets per share for June 2026: RM7.86, up from RM7.62). Most assets are ships and offshore units on long contracts.

safety.label: Cash from operations 1H2026
safety.plain: Up 52.5% from RM2,375m a year earlier, mainly from the tanker business.

safety.label: Borrowings (Dec 2025)
safety.plain: Down from RM15,494m after repaying USD400m of notes in 2025.

safety.label: Net debt to equity (Dec 2025)
safety.plain: Borrowings minus cash are only a fifth of shareholders' funds: low for a shipping company.

safety.label: Interest cover (FY2025)
safety.plain: Earnings before interest and tax cover interest costs about 4 times.

safety.label: Committed capital spending (Dec 2025)
safety.plain: Ships and projects already ordered or contracted, to be paid over coming years.

safetyTitle: Cash and debt at a glance
safetyIntro: MISC's annual report and results release give these cash and debt figures; full statements are filed separately. Tap a card to see what it means.

metrics.label: Market value
metrics.plain: What the whole company costs at today's share price: RM34.5 billion.

metrics.label: P/E (last 12 months)
metrics.plain: You pay about RM14 for every RM1 of yearly profit. A high number means investors expect growth.

metrics.label: EPS (last 12 months)
metrics.plain: Profit earned for each share you own over the last year.

metrics.label: Dividend yield (FY2025 dividends)
metrics.plain: For every RM100 of shares, about RM4.9 a year comes back as cash dividends.

metrics.label: Payout ratio
metrics.plain: Of every RM100 profit, about RM70 is paid out; the rest is kept to grow.

metrics.label: Price to book
metrics.plain: The share price is 1.0 times the accounting value of what shareholders own.

metrics.label: Return on equity (last 12 months)
metrics.plain: For every RM100 shareholders have in the company, it earned about RM7 profit last year.

metrics.label: Net margin 1H2026
metrics.plain: What is left as profit for shareholders from every RM100 of revenue: RM24.67.

metrics.label: Revenue growth 1H2026
metrics.plain: Revenue compared with the same period a year earlier.

metrics.label: Profit growth 1H2026
metrics.plain: Profit to shareholders compared with the same period a year earlier.

metrics.label: Net debt
metrics.plain: Borrowings minus cash: RM6.78 billion owed to lenders after using all its cash.

metrics.label: Net gearing
metrics.plain: Net debt is 20% of shareholders' funds. Under 50% is usually seen as comfortable; above 100% means lenders fund more than owners.

metrics.label: Interest cover (FY2025)
metrics.plain: Earnings before interest and tax cover interest costs about 4 times (AR p.75).

drivers.evidence: Elevated crude tanker rates drove an exceptional second quarter for the Petroleum business (PR)
drivers.why: The biggest swing factor in 2026 profit.

drivers.evidence: Management is 'measured' about 2H2026: the Petroleum contribution may moderate (PR)
drivers.why: Spot rates can fall as fast as they rose.

drivers.evidence: Two LNG carriers delivered and started long-term charters with SeaRiver Maritime (PR)
drivers.why: Locks in income for many years.

drivers.evidence: Gas revenue fell on disposals, lay-ups and lower rates; older vessels depreciated faster (PR)
drivers.why: Old steam-turbine ships struggle to find work.

drivers.evidence: Higher construction revenue from an FSO and a floating production unit (PR)
Operational shutdown of an FPSO weighed on offshore profit in 1H2026 (PR)
drivers.why: Lost days on a large earning asset.

drivers.evidence: Heavy engineering projects moved into higher construction phases (PR)
drivers.why: Higher yard revenue and repair demand from LNG carrier dry-docking.

drivers.evidence: Gains on disposing of ships boosted 2Q2026 profit (PR)
drivers.why: One-off gains that may not repeat.

drivers.evidence: Uncertainty around the Strait of Hormuz expected to keep spot rates volatile (PR)
drivers.why: Can lift rates but raises risk to ships and crews.

drivers.evidence: Second long-term CO2 carrier charter with Northern Lights JV (PR)
drivers.why: A new market in the energy transition.

drivers.evidence: Net debt/equity 0.20x and interest cover 3.9x at end-2025 (AR p.75)
16 sen paid for 1H2026; 38 sen for FY2025 (PR; AR p.73)
About 14 times last-12-month profit at RM7.72 (see Valuation)
drivers.why: Cheaper than a year ago thanks to higher profit, but tanker profits are cyclical.

suppliers: Build its new LNG carriers, tankers and carbon-dioxide carriers; MHB signed an MoU with Hanwha Power Systems on newbuilding projects
Employment costs of RM2.3bn in FY2025
Part of RM4.7bn of goods and services bought in FY2025
Banks and bond investors: RM12.9bn of borrowings at end-2025
customers: Long-term charters for LNG carriers and a floating regasification unit for PETRONAS Gas
LNG carrier charters with SeaRiver Maritime; an FSO in Papua New Guinea for ExxonMobil PNG
Northern Lights JV: two long-term carbon-dioxide carrier charters
Tanker voyages at market (spot) rates and on contracts through AET
supply.note: MISC is part of the PETRONAS group, which is both a major customer and its controlling shareholder. The sources do not give each customer's share of revenue.

competitors.name: Large shipping and LNG carrier owners (e.g. NYK, MOL, K Line, Teekay)
competitors.how: Compete for long-term gas and oil shipping charters
competitors.source: General market knowledge, not the report

competitors.name: FPSO contractors (e.g. SBM Offshore, MODEC, BW Offshore)
Regional shipyards in Singapore, Korea and China
competitors.how: Compete for offshore fabrication and ship repair

outlook.text: Strong LNG supply growth, especially from the Americas, supports long-term LNG carrier charter rates (PR).
Offshore expected to stay resilient on a strong pipeline of FPSO awards in Asia, South America and Africa (PR).
Measured expectations for 2H2026: the strong Petroleum contribution may moderate (PR).
Geopolitical uncertainty and the Strait of Hormuz will keep spot rates volatile; older steam-turbine LNG carriers face pressure (PR).

outlookOverall.text: Management reports an exceptional first half and long-term contract wins, but is measured about the second half (PR).
